claim: The first noun heads a number of protesters, with number transparency where appropriate.
evidence_summary: Movement of of whom comes from a true partitive. This number of people come also challenges a simple second-noun analysis.
finding: Partitive movement does not distinguish the two proposed structures for the pseudopartitive.
inference: Does moving the PP in a true partitive locate the head of a pseudopartitive?

evidence.source: Frank Van Eynde & Jong-Bok Kim (2023). Pseudo-partitives in English: An HPSG analysis. English Language & Linguistics 27(2), 271–302.
evidence.passage: §3.3, p. 349. The first noun heads a number of protesters, with number transparency where appropriate.
evidence.example: The article develops a second-noun-headed account and gives a great deal of people in (60), from a 2012 blog in COCA.
evidence.establishes: A lexical restriction can fail regardless of which head analysis wins. The published corpus example bears specifically on CG-0008.
evidence.locator: Alternative headedness analysis. For the narrower oblique-number issue, p. 294 (60).
